contentFull:
Broiler farmers test biochar to tackle ammonia emissions

A group of broiler farmers across the West Midlands is taking a practical approach to one of the poultry sector’s biggest environmental and management challenges by testing whether engineered biochar can reduce ammonia emissions and improve litter quality in commercial sheds.

Tony McDougalFreelance journalist

Aug 20

News

Engineered biochar is being tested as a poultry bedding additive to assess its potential to reduce ammonia emissions and improve litter quality. Image created with the help of AI. 

The project, funded through the ADOPT programme, brings together producers in Shropshire, Herefordshire and Worcestershire with researchers and biochar specialists to evaluate the technology under real farm conditions.

While biochar has attracted increasing attention within agriculture, its use in poultry housing remains relatively unexplored, making the trial particularly relevant for producers looking for workable solutions to improve shed conditions.

Farmers lead the research

At the centre of the project is farmer and project lead Rob Collins, who believes the value of the work lies in generating robust evidence that other poultry producers can trust.

“Farmers are under increasing pressure to manage ammonia emissions while maintaining bird welfare and performance,” he says. “We wanted to test whether engineered biochar could provide a practical solution that fits into everyday farm management rather than creating additional complexity.”

ALSO READ: Smart cameras reveal how broilers respond to heat stress and ageing

The trial focuses on applying engineered biochar directly to poultry bedding. The material is produced from spruce wood through a pyrolysis process that creates a stable and highly porous product capable of absorbing and holding nutrients.

Across 4 commercial broiler farms, researchers have installed ammonia sensors to capture real-time data throughout each crop cycle. Farmers will also assess litter condition, handling characteristics and any observable changes in bird welfare.

Collins says the multi-farm approach is one of the strengths of the project: “Every poultry unit is slightly different. By running the trial across several farms we can see how biochar performs under a range of management systems and shed environments.”

Testing biochar under commercial conditions

For biochar specialist Kevin Fryer, who has worked with the material for more than 3 decades, the project represents an opportunity to demonstrate what high-quality engineered biochar can achieve in a commercial setting.

“There has been growing interest in biochar for many years, but farmers need evidence they can rely on,” he says. “This trial allows us to evaluate performance in working poultry sheds and understand whether the benefits suggested by earlier work can be replicated consistently.”

ALSO READ: Can canola offer lower-cost alternative to soybean meal for broilers?

Dr David Redpath, an academic specialising in sustainable utilisation of livestock by-products, believes taking research out of controlled environments and into commercial enterprises is essential. He says applied research is most valuable when it reflects the realities of farming and will help the team understand how engineered biochar performs under genuine production conditions.

Results expected later this year

The team says ADOPT has made innovation funding more accessible and easier for farmers to navigate. Participants also highlight the value of facilitator support in coordinating partners and managing project administration.

Although results are not expected until later this year, the group hopes the project will provide clear evidence on whether engineered biochar can help reduce ammonia emissions, improve litter quality and create better conditions for birds.

If successful, it could offer poultry producers a practical new tool for improving sustainability while supporting welfare and operational efficiency.
translationZh:
西米德兰兹郡的一群肉鸡养殖户正在采取一种务实的方法来应对家禽业最大的环境和管理挑战之一，他们正在测试工程生物炭能否在商业鸡舍中减少氨气排放并改善垫料质量。

该项目由ADOPT计划资助，汇集了什罗普郡、赫里福德郡和伍斯特郡的生产者，与研究人员和生物炭专家合作，在真实农场条件下评估这项技术。

虽然生物炭在农业中日益受到关注，但其在家禽舍内的应用仍相对未被探索，这使得该试验对寻求改善鸡舍条件的可行解决方案的生产者尤其具有相关性。

**农民主导研究**

项目的核心是农民兼项目负责人罗伯·柯林斯，他认为这项工作的价值在于生成其他家禽生产者可以信赖的可靠证据。

“农民在管理氨气排放的同时维持鸟类福利和生产性能方面面临越来越大的压力，”他说。“我们想测试工程生物炭是否能提供一种实用的解决方案，融入日常农场管理，而不是增加额外的复杂性。”

**另请阅读：** 智能摄像头揭示肉鸡如何应对热应激和老龄化

试验的重点是将工程生物炭直接应用于家禽垫料。该材料由云杉木通过热解过程制成，形成一种稳定且高度多孔的产品，能够吸收和保留营养物质。

在4个商业肉鸡农场，研究人员安装了氨气传感器，以在每个生产周期内捕获实时数据。农民还将评估垫料状况、处理特性以及鸟类福利的任何可观察变化。

柯林斯表示，多农场方法是该项目的一大优势：“每个家禽单位都略有不同。通过在多个农场进行试验，我们可以看到生物炭在各种管理系统和鸡舍环境中的表现。”

**在商业条件下测试生物炭**

对于从事生物炭工作超过30年的生物炭专家凯文·弗莱尔来说，该项目是展示高质量工程生物炭在商业环境中能实现什么的机会。

“多年来，人们对生物炭的兴趣日益浓厚，但农民需要他们可以依赖的证据，”他说。“这项试验使我们能够在实际家禽舍中评估性能，并了解早期工作提出的益处是否能够一致地复制。”

**另请阅读：** 菜籽能否成为肉鸡豆粕的低成本替代品？

专门研究牲畜副产品可持续利用的学者戴维·雷德帕斯博士认为，将研究从受控环境带入商业企业至关重要。他说，应用研究在反映农业现实时最有价值，并将帮助团队了解工程生物炭在真实生产条件下的表现。

**结果预计今年晚些时候公布**

团队表示，ADOPT使创新资金更容易获得，也更容易让农民驾驭。参与者还强调了协调伙伴关系和管理项目行政的促进者支持的价值。

尽管结果预计要到今年晚些时候才能公布，但该团队希望该项目能提供明确的证据，证明工程生物炭是否有助于减少氨气排放、改善垫料质量并为鸟类创造更好的条件。

如果成功，它可能为家禽生产者提供一种实用的新工具，以提高可持续性，同时支持福利和运营效率。
author: Tony McDougal
